ei.title: Chapter 4-10 1번: The Flexible Boundaries of Social Bonds
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have ①<u>evolved</u> to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be ②<u>rather</u> flexible. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute ④<u>certain</u> human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: they(복수 주어)의 보어 자리이므로 복수 명사 members가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
① evolved — have evolved, 현재완료 p.p. 정상
② rather — 부사, rather flexible 정상
③ as if they are member — 원문 members, 복수 주어 they의 보어로 복수 명사 필요 ←정답
④ certain — 형용사, certain human characteristics 정상
det.tip: 복수 주어 + be + 복수 보어: they are members

det.korean: think of 뒤에는 동명사(talking)가 와야 한다. to talk는 전치사 of의 목적어로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:

② to talk — 원문 talking, 전치사 of 뒤 동명사 필요 ←정답

④ attribute — 동사원형, still attribute 정상
det.tip: 전치사 + 동명사: think of talking (think of to talk 비문)

For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can ②<u>relate</u> to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if ③<u>which</u> was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a ④<u>deceased</u> loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: as if 뒤에 주어+동사가 오는 완전한 절이다. which는 관계대명사로 선행사가 필요하므로 이 자리에 부적합. 대명사 it이 올바르다.
det.analysis:
① defining — 동명사 주어, defining what should be 정상
② relate — 조동사 can + 원형동사, can relate to 정상
③ which — 원문 it, as if 뒤 완전한 절에 주어 대명사 it 필요. which는 관계대명사로 선행사 없이 불가 ←정답
④ deceased — 형용사, a deceased loved one 정상
det.tip: as if it was a friend: it(대명사) = one(= an animal). 관계대명사 which는 부적절.

For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can ②<u>object</u> to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as ③<u>distinct</u> from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, ④<u>believing</u> those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '반대하다(object)'가 아니라 '공감하다(relate)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 반려동물의 욕구에 공감할 수 있다고 믿는다.
det.analysis:
① evolved — 진화하다, 원문 일치
② object — 원문 relate, 반려동물에 '공감'하는 맥락 ←정답
③ distinct — 구별되는, 원문 일치
④ believing — 믿으면서, 원문 일치
det.tip: relate to(공감하다) ↔ object to(반대하다)

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but ①<u>defining</u> what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people ②<u>treat</u> their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to ③<u>serve</u> as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us ④<u>never</u> attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '절대 ~하지 않는다(never)'가 아니라 '여전히(still)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 무생물에도 인간적 특성을 '여전히' 부여한다.
det.analysis:
① defining — 정의하는, 원문 일치
② treat — 대하다, 원문 일치
③ serve — 역할을 하다, 원문 일치
④ never — 원문 still, '여전히 부여한다'가 맥락 ←정답
det.tip: still(여전히) ↔ never(절대 ~않다): 글의 핵심 논지가 반전됨

questions.passage: Our complex brains might have evolved to establish strong social bonds, but defining what should be part of that social group appears to be rather flexible. For instance, some people treat their pets __________, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as some link to their existence. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean:
어떤 사람들은 반려동물을 마치 가족 구성원인 것처럼(as if they are members of their family) 대한다.

(빈칸추론 2단어+ 충족: 9단어 구절)
det.analysis:
① as if they are members of their family — 가족처럼, 뒤에 욕구·두려움에 공감한다는 내용과 연결 ←정답
② as though they lack any emotion — 감정이 없는 것처럼, 공감 맥락과 모순
③ because they are merely property — 재산에 불과하므로, 가족처럼 대하는 맥락과 반대
④ unless they behave like humans — 인간처럼 행동하지 않는 한, 조건절로 문맥 부적합
det.tip: treat A as if ~ = A를 마치 ~인 것처럼 대하다

ch: as if they are members of their family
as though they lack any emotion

For instance, some people treat their pets as if they are members of their family, and believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears and dreams. Others see animals as distinct from humans and wouldn't think of talking to one as if it was a friend. Many people keep the ashes of a deceased loved one nearby, believing those ashes continue to serve as __________. Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean:
유골이 고인의 존재에 대한 어떤 연결고리(some link to their existence) 역할을 한다고 믿는다.

(빈칸추론 2단어+ 충족: 5단어 구절)
det.analysis:
① an obstacle to social bonding — 사회적 유대의 장애물(유골 보관 맥락과 무관)
② a threat to their well-being — 안녕에 대한 위협(부정적 의미, 본문과 불일치)
③ some link to their existence — 존재에 대한 연결고리 ←정답
④ a burden on the living — 살아있는 자의 짐(본문에 부정적 판단 없음)
det.tip: serve as some link to their existence = 존재에 대한 연결고리 역할

Even if inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality, many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings, such as pets, dolls or even cars and memorabilia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: many of us still attribute certain human characteristics to non-human objects or beings
det.analysis:
① establish strong social bonds → 형성(강화) 방향 (약화 아님)
② rather flexible → 유연함 (고정적 아님)
③ Others wouldn't think of talking → 모든 사람 아님
④ attribute human characteristics to non-human objects — 일치 ←정답
det.tip: attribute ~ to non-human objects = 비인간 대상에 인간적 특성 부여

ch: 뇌의 진화는 사회적 유대를 약화시키는 방향으로 이루어졌다.
사회 집단의 구성원 범위는 고정적이고 변하지 않는다.
동물에게 말을 건네는 행위는 모든 사람에게 자연스러운 일이다.
무생물 대상에 인간적 특성을 부여하는 사람들이 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 'believe they can relate'이라고 하여 '믿는다'고 서술했지, '단정'한 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
① 글쓴이가 '단정'한다 → believe(믿다)이지 단정이 아님 ←정답(불일치)
② believe they can relate to the pets' needs, desires, fears — 일치
③ keep the ashes nearby — 일치
④ such as pets, dolls or even cars — 일치
det.tip: believe(~라고 믿다) ≠ 단정(assert/claim definitively)

ch: 글쓴이는 동물에게 인간적 감정이 있다고 단정한다.
어떤 사람들은 반려동물의 두려움이나 욕구에 공감한다고 믿는다.
고인의 유골을 가까이 보관하는 사람들이 있다.
인형이나 자동차도 인간적 특성이 부여되는 대상에 포함된다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문은 'inanimate objects don't have a distinct personality'라고 하여 성격이 '없음에도 불구하고' 부여한다고 서술한다.
det.analysis:

② believing those ashes serve as some link — 일치
③ 성격을 갖고 있어서 → don't have, 본문은 '성격이 없는데도' 부여 ←정답(불일치)
④ memorabilia — 일치
det.tip: Even if ~ don't have = ~이 없더라도 (양보 접속사)

ch: 사회 집단에 속할 대상을 정의하는 것은 유연한 편이다.
유골이 고인의 존재와의 연결 역할을 한다고 믿는 사람이 있다.
무생물은 뚜렷한 성격을 갖고 있어서 인간적 특성이 부여된다.
기념품도 인간적 특성이 부여되는 비인간 대상의 예시에 포함된다.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 some link to their existence가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean:
'존재에 대한 어떤 연결'은 유골을 통해 고인과의 정서적 연결이 유지된다는 심리적 믿음을 의미한다.

→ 본문: believing(믿으면서) — 주관적 믿음임을 명시
det.analysis:
① 물리적 존재가 남아있다 — 비유적 표현을 문자적으로 해석 (×)
② 정서적·심리적 연결 유지의 믿음 ←정답
③ 다시 살아올 수 있다 — 본문에 부활 언급 없음
④ DNA 보존 — 과학적 사실이 아닌 심리적 믿음
det.tip: link = 연결고리, believing = 믿으면서 → 주관적 정서적 연결

ch: 고인의 물리적 존재가 유골 속에 그대로 남아있다는 사실
